body.name: bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class \(\mathfrak Q(P)\)
body.construction:
The bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity completion class is
\[
\mathfrak Q(P)=\left\{Q:\begin{array}{l}
Q\text{ is a law over the declared one-argument static schedules and matches the entire observed law }P;\\
\text{consistency and latent integrability hold; }g\in C(H);\\
\text{the simultaneous common-event conditional-parallel-trends condition holds on }X_0;\\
\left|E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z]\right|\le K|Z|\quad Q\text{-almost surely};\\
m_Q\in C(X_0),\quad \|m_Q\|_\infty\le M,\quad
|m_Q(x)-m_Q(x')|\le L|x-x'|\quad\text{for all }x,x'\in X_0
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
No marginal quasi-stayer restriction is part of this definition.  The finite \(K\) movement bound, the bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz trend, the continuous support version \(g\), and the simultaneous common-event clause are explicit sensitivity restrictions.  On an observed law satisfying the published assumptions, comparison with the source class concerns only source completions that also satisfy these restrictions.  No global equality or inclusion of completion classes is asserted, and the finite sharp interval for this sensitivity class does not transfer upward to the unrestricted published class.
